A dimensionless measure of mechanical vulnerability to hydrodynamic disturbance (see Madin and Connolly 2006).  Colony shape factor is a function of colony size, and therefore each observation should also include a colony size measurement. Currently published data is only available for three species.
The swimming speed, typically the maximum, of coral larvae.
The CaCO3 polymorph found in the skeleton, without considering sclerites
The CaCO3 polymorph present in sclerites (mostly calcite but Aragonite and Vaterite in some species)
The Mg/Ca ratio in sclerites

The concentration of MgCO3 in sclerites
For species with axis only. The concentration of Mg in axis
The material density of coral skeleton. Porosity measurements can be converted to density by multiplying the reciprocal of porosity by the maximum density of aragonite (2.94 g cm^-3).

The fine-scale specific gravity of the material from which coral skeleton is constructed (Bucher et al. 1998, following terminology from Barnes & Devereux 1988). Micro-density should be closer to the density of solid aragonite (~2.96 g cm^-3) than to typical bulk densities, because it does not capture corallite voids (i.e., porosity).

The rigidity of a coral colony or individual, based on the type of skeleton. Allowed values are:  Soft (i.e., species with just a hydrostatic skeleton in which the whole colony is capable of retracting or deflating or greatly changing its volume), Semi-rigid (i.e., species with an axis in which the colony itself is not capable of retraction/deflation) and rigid (i.e., species with a totally hard skeleton that is heavily calcified).
A mechanical property of materials that measures the  stiffness when the force is applied lengthwise
Whether or not individuals attach to substrates, including reef, rock and wood.
